newsitem.title: USA: Brunswick to buy Life Fitness for $310 million.
newsitem.headline: Brunswick to buy Life Fitness for $310 million.

text.p: Brunswick Corp. said Wednesday it agreed to buy exercise equipment maker Life Fitness for about $310 million from a private equity fund managed by Mancuso & Co., a New York merchant banking firm.

Life Fitness, based in Franklin Park, Ill., manufactures computerized cardiovascular and strength training fitness equipment for health clubs and other facilities and the high-end consumer market. Its products include the Lifecycle stationary bicycle.
Life Fitness, with annual sales of about $180 million, also markets treadmills, stairclimbers, rowers, cross trainers and strength training equipment to fitness centres world wide.
The deal is scheduled to close in July. The business will continue to be operated by its current management.
"Life Fitness fits perfectly with the strategy Brunswick is executing," Chairman Peter Larson said in a statement.
The recreational products maker, based in Lake Forest, Ill., is best known for its Brunswick bowling equipment and family entertainment centres, and Brunswick billiard tables.

"We have targeted the active recreation segment due to favourable demographic and consumer trends, such as baby boomers remaining more active as they move into their 50's with more spendable income and the emphasis on wellness, active lifestyles and social interaction," Larson said.
Brunswick also sees growth opportunities for Life Fitness as physicians promote exercise to treat and reduce the risk of disease, as well as in international markets, he said.

Brunswick also makes Zebco and Quantum fishing reels; American Camper and Remington camping gear; Igloo coolers and ice chests; Mongoose, Roadmaster and Ride Hard bicycles; Sea Ray, Bayliner and Maxum pleasure boats; Baja boats; Boston Whaler and Trophy offshore fishing boats; Mercury, Mariner and Force outboard engines and MerCruiser sterndrives and inboard engines.
Brunswick's stock fell 12.5 cents to $30 early on the New York Stock Exchange.
